newsitem.title: CHINA: SMALL BANK STOCKS SURGE ON HK MORTGAGE RATE HIKE.
newsitem.headline: SMALL BANK STOCKS SURGE ON HK MORTGAGE RATE HIKE.

text.p: Shares of small Hong Kong banks jumped on Wednesday as investors hoped for a better earnings outlook following a recent rise in mortgage rates by major banks, brokers said.
"Investors are anticipating an increase in net interest margins due to the mortgage rate hike," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Hongkong Bank and Standard Chartered Bank raised their mortgage rates by 25 basis points to 9.25 percent recently, fuelling speculation of similar moves by smaller banks.
Shares of Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd rose HK$1.65, or 8.64 percent, to HK$20.75 in late trade and Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd gained HK$1.20, or 6.03 percent, to HK$21.10.
Ka Wah Bank gained HK$1.25, or 13.23 percent, to HK$10.70 and Dao Heng Bank was up HK$1.10 to HK$46.50.
"A slight rebound in HSBC shares after the recent correction also gave investors a buy signal," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.00 to HK$274. Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.50 to HK$107.
